name: India–Pakistan
value: Airspace ban to 23 Nov; no strikes
summary: Pakistan's airspace ban on Indian aircraft runs to 23 Nov and the Indus treaty dispute continues; no strike found
state: Pakistan's ban on Indian-operated aircraft in its airspace was renewed to 23 Nov (Airways Magazine), and India's suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty remains disputed after a Hague arbitration ruling (Pakistan Observer). Searches on 11 Nov found no new Line of Control incident, cross-border military strike or mobilisation. Ongoing treaty suspensions keep the signal at Watch.
for_you: Flights between India, Pakistan and the Gulf may take longer routes while airspace bans last. Travellers can follow FCDO travel advice for India and Pakistan.
rubric_hit: Treaty suspensions and airspace bans in place = Watch; no cross-border strikes or mobilisation

sources.title: Airways Magazine — Pakistan Extends Indian Aircraft Airspace Ban Until November 24
Pakistan Observer — column on the Indus Waters Treaty ruling

why: Two nuclear-armed neighbours with a history of rapid escalation after terrorist attacks.
drivers: Kashmir attacks, Line of Control firing, water disputes (Indus), domestic politics.

rubric.watch: Ceasefire violations, a major terrorist attack with blame assigned, or treaty suspensions.
rubric.normal: Ceasefire holding along the Line of Control; no major attacks.
